To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recombinant baculovirus-expressed form of AcMNPV gp64 is a soluble protein with mixed alpha- and beta-helical content and that it forms a trimeric structure in solution and at pH 5 that does not bind to insect cells.
the soluble form of the Autgraphica californica gp64 protein was a trimer that did not bind to the cell surface and that the deglycosylate form of the protein crystallized.
a soluble form of the major baculovirus envelope glycoprotein, Gp64, is a trimeric protein that does not bind to the cell surface, suggesting that it may have a novel mechanism for virus-cell fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of baculovirus infection.
the molecular mechanisms of baculovirus infection and how they differ from those of other viruses.
the structure and function of a baculovirus glycoprotein that mediates virus-cell fusion, a process that may be important to the development of novel viral vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gp64 protein is an important fusion protein, which has been shown to be a trimer in the native state, and is a promising candidate for structural studies.
the soluble gp64 protein has a mixed alpha-helix/beta-sheet secondary structure, is a trimer in its native state and is not involved in virus-cell fusion.
this soluble form of gp64 has a novel mechanism of fusion and may form the basis for a structural study.
